--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MPJBWDJSX6PEP6N39XRXNP
+- 01M1MPGFG6DKJFC7T3R24Q3M8S
+- 01M1MPKCCB56CA910R6JA5XSFA
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9280'
+title: Record the CLI decisions in cli-plan.md and README.md
+---
+## What
+
+Three decisions were made while planning this work, and two of them contradict
+what `cli-plan.md` says today. A plan that disagrees with the code is worse
+than no plan.
+
+Edit `cli-plan.md`:
+
+- **§5.** The family takes Noora directly, with no spike. Replace the sentence
+  that says this package follows the agent package's C1 result, and say that
+  the decision is made here and the agent package follows it. Keep the rule
+  that the terminal package writes to stderr only.
+- **§13 and §16.** Terminal authentication stays out, as §13 already says. No
+  change is needed to the decision; check the section still reads true after
+  the work and leave it as it is.
+- **New section, permission and elicitation.** `acp-client` advertises
+  `ACPClient.advertisedCapabilities`, which advertises elicitation in both
+  modes, so a foreign agent may ask. The binary declines every permission
+  request and every elicitation, and writes one stderr line for each. Give the
+  reason: a headless one-turn binary has no person to ask, and a batch run
+  must never grant an agent something a person did not see. Note that an
+  interactive policy is a later question, and add it to §16.
+- **§7.** Add a note that the binary resolves a bare agent command through
+  `PATH` itself, because `AgentProcess` accepts an absolute path only.
+- **§8.** Add a note that the turn ends on the `idle` `state_update`, and not
+  on the prompt acknowledgement, because `PromptResponse` in v2 carries no
+  stop reason.
+- **§15.** Mark N5 as free of an upstream block: the `Doctorable` module in
+  `FoundationModelsExtras` is present under
+  `Sources/FoundationModelsExtras/Doctor/`.
+
+Edit `README.md`: the package is a library landing page today. Add one short
+section that names `acp-client`, gives the two example invocations of §6, and
+says the binary is a product an other package may depend on.
+
+Write every change in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, matching the
+style already in `cli-plan.md`.
+
+`FoundationModelsACPAgent/cli-plan.md` §5.2 and its milestone C1 also need the
+Noora decision. That is an other repository, so do not edit it here: name it in
+the pull request description instead.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `cli-plan.md` §5 states the Noora decision as made, with no reference to
+      a pending spike.
+- [ ] `cli-plan.md` holds a section for the decline policy, with its reason.
+- [ ] `cli-plan.md` §15 no longer says N5 is blocked.
+- [ ] `cli-plan.md` §16 names the interactive permission policy as an open
+      item.
+- [ ] `README.md` names `acp-client` and shows two invocations.
+- [ ] No statement in `cli-plan.md` contradicts the shipped code.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] New `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/PlanDocumentTests.swift`,
+      built on the existing `RepositoryFile.read(relativePath:)` helper. It
+      asserts `cli-plan.md` holds the decline-policy section heading, that
+      §15 does not hold the word "Blocked" on the N5 row, and that
+      `README.md` names `acp-client`. These pin the facts a later edit could
+      silently drop.
+- [ ] One test asserts every subcommand name that `cli-plan.md` §6 lists is a
+      subcommand `AcpClient.configuration` declares, so the document and the
+      parser cannot drift.
+- [ ] One test asserts every exit code in the §9 table appears in
+      `AcpClientExitCode`, read from the document and compared with
+      `allCases`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. Every assertion passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
